correctness.rationale: Finite-dimensional strong LP duality proves the exact coordinate identity norm because the hereditary source constraints restrict to each target finite set and singleton constraints guarantee primal/dual feasibility. For graph clique families these are precisely complement independent-set constraints; the inverse ell1-to-X_G is contractive and has norm 1, hence a bounded identity extends to an onto isomorphism. An odd cycle on 2m+1 vertices gives an explicit dual fractional chromatic lower bound 2+1/m, while absence of odd cycles is equivalent to bipartiteness, proving the exact threshold. For each c>2 the disjoint union of Kneser KG(floor(ck),k) as the complementary graph is implemented by complete joins of intersection graph blocks of total cardinal omega_1. On each block star averaging gives an upper operator bound floor(ck)/k; uniform coefficients plus the published Erdos–Ko–Rado intersection bound attain it. Supremizing over k yields exact c, and the published Lovasz–Kneser formula gives complement chromatic number aleph_0. Finite-support block norm additivity plus density proves all infinite-dimensional extensions. No finite experiment substitutes for the graph theorems.

value.rationale: The recent theory explicitly asks which analytic properties of arbitrary-cardinality combinatorial spaces can be read from their finite-set combinatorics. This finding gives a natural exact universal graph-theoretic invariant for a canonical ell1-equivalence problem, valid in nonseparable cardinalities. Its sharp qualitative phase transition is structurally motivated: at distortion 2 the whole complement must be bipartite and a partition into at most two cliques exists, while any arbitrarily small larger distortion permits countably infinite minimal clique-cover number even on omega_1 with ell1 isomorphism. The theorem is a complete comparison classification and parameter-complete boundary realization, not a standalone finite table or routine variable substitution. The older integer-star precursor is acknowledged and the value lies specifically in the graph-clique fractional/integral separation.
